headline: Rubio emphasizes U.S. national interest primacy, rejects ICC authority, frames Iran nuclear capability as civilizational threat
facts: Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered remarks at Federalist Society's 2026 National Lawyers Convention on November 13, 2026, at Mayflower Hotel, Washington D.C.
Rubio stated President Trump sanctioned the International Criminal Court (ICC) in 2026, describing it as 'fake' and 'unelected world tribunal'
Rubio cited President Reagan's approval rating decline: from 68% to 43% (25-point drop) in early 1982, reaching 4 points below Jimmy Carter's approval at equivalent term point

Rubio referenced Federalist Society founding: April 1982 law school symposium in New Haven, Connecticut, organized by four law students with ~200 attendees; Antonin Scalia (then 46-year-old Chicago professor) was keynote speaker
Rubio stated Roe v. Wade decision (nine years before 1982 = 1973): 5 of 7 votes were Republican appointees; majority opinion written by Nixon nominee
Rubio noted: at 1982 time of Federalist Society founding, only Harvard Law School had a conservative student journal (founded 4 years prior = 1978)
Term 'originalism' coined two years before 1982 (1980) by liberal Stanford professor in article criticizing the concept
U.S. territorial expansion: 1776 (13 states on eastern coast) to 1848 (72 years later) — continental empire spanning nearly 3 million square miles
Rubio stated Iran has 'been waging war on the United States since 1979'
Rubio cited Hizballah bombing: killed over 280 American Marines in 1982-1983 (barracks bombing)
Rubio referenced Hizballah bombing Buenos Aires Jewish center in early 1990s in Western Hemisphere
Rubio stated Iran is 'world's leading sponsor of terrorism' — no nation-state in history has spent more time/money sponsoring terrorism globally
Rubio stated current Strait of Hormuz situation: 13-14 million barrels passing through nightly despite Iranian attacks on ships
watchlist: ICC 제재의 실질적 집행 메커니즘 및 국제적 반발 수준
